question: As per IS 10500:2012, what is the permissible limit (in the absence of an alternative source) for arsenic in drinking water?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 0.005 mg/L is the WHO guideline value; IS 10500:2012 permits a higher relaxed limit when no alternative source is available.
0.01 mg/L is the desirable limit (acceptable limit) under IS 10500:2012.
Correct. IS 10500:2012 sets 0.05 mg/L as the permissible limit in the absence of an alternate source, with 0.01 mg/L as the acceptable limit.
0.1 mg/L exceeds the permissible limit for arsenic under any Indian standard.

overallFeedback.feedback: IS 10500:2012 sets the acceptable limit at 0.01 mg/L and permissible relaxed limit at 0.05 mg/L for arsenic. This matters for endemic areas like West Bengal and Bangladesh border districts.
Correct! IS 10500:2012 allows up to 0.05 mg/L arsenic as a permissible limit (when no alternative exists), though the acceptable limit is 0.01 mg/L.
